'''Antony Garrett Lisi''' (born January 24, 1968) is an American theoretical physicist whose research focuses on [[differential geometry]], [[mathematical physics]], and [[quantum gravity]]. He is known for his 2007 proposal, [[An Exceptionally Simple Theory of Everything]], which sought to unify gravity and the [[Standard Model of particle physics]] using the [[Simple Lie group|exceptional Lie group]] [[E8]]. The theory has been extensively criticized in the scientific community.<ref name="cbc-2007-11-16">{{cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/science/surfer-makes-waves-with-scientific-theory-of-everything-1.672697|title=Surfer makes waves with scientific 'theory of everything'|publisher=CBC News|date=November 16, 2007|access-date=July 2, 2008|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080611112752/http://www.cbc.ca/technology/story/2007/11/16/science-theory-everything.html|archive-date=11 June 2008}}</ref><ref name="Collins-2008-03">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.sciam.com/article.cfm?id=wipeout-theory|title=Wipeout?|magazine=[[Scientific American]]|date=March 2008|pages=30–32|last=Collins|first=Graham P.|access-date=June 18, 2008}}</ref><ref name="Distler-Garibaldi-2010">{{cite journal|author1=J.Distler|author1-link=Jacques Distler|author2=S. Garibaldi|author2-link=Skip Garibaldi|name-list-style=amp|year=2010|title=There is no "Theory of Everything" inside E{{sub|8}}|journal=[[Communications in Mathematical Physics]]|volume=298|pages=419–436|doi=10.1007/s00220-010-1006-y|arxiv=0905.2658|issue=2|bibcode=2010CMaPh.298..419D|s2cid=15074118}}</ref><ref name=Sifter-2008>{{cite web|url=http://sifter.org/~aglisi/a.html|title='A' (What, like as opposed to '''''the''''' Garrett Lisi?)|website=sifter.org|date=July 5, 2008|last=Lisi|first=A.G.|access-date=July 5, 2008|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080523213610/http://sifter.org/~aglisi/a.html|archive-date=23 May 2008}}</ref> 

==Biography==
===Education and career===
Lisi was born in Los Angeles and raised in San Diego, California.<ref name="fox">{{cite news|first=Jim|last=Patton|date=November 15, 2007|title='Physics is beautiful' and a few other thoughts from Garrett Lisi|publisher=Fox News|url=http://blogs.fox6.com/blogs/balancedviews/archive/2007/11/20/2194296.aspx|access-date=July 2, 2008}}</ref> He graduated from [[Cate School]] in 1987.<ref name=Weatherall-2008>{{cite magazine|first=James Owen|last=Weatherall|date=June 1, 2008|title=No strings attached|magazine=Men's Journal}}</ref> Lisi went on to receive two [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] degrees with highest honors in physics and mathematics from the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], in 1991. Lisi received a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in physics from the [[University of California, San Diego]], in 1999.<ref name=Dance-2008>{{cite magazine|first=Amber|last=Dance|date=April 1, 2008|title=Outsider science|magazine=Symmetry Magazine|url=http://www.symmetrymagazine.org/cms/?pid=1000607|url-status=dead|access-date=June 15, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080705195339/http://www.symmetrymagazine.org/cms/?pid=1000607|archive-date=5 July 2008}}</ref>  Lisi then left academia.<ref name=Carroll-2007>{{cite web|first=Sean|last=Carroll|date=July 6, 2008|title=Garrett Lisi's theory of everything|website=Cosmic Variance|url=http://cosmicvariance.com/2007/11/16/garrett-lisis-theory-of-everything/|access-date=July 6, 2008|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080623064238/http://cosmicvariance.com/2007/11/16/garrett-lisis-theory-of-everything/|archive-date=23 June 2008}}</ref>

In July 2006, Lisi was awarded an [[FQXi]] grant to conduct research in quantum mechanics and unification.<ref name="FQXi-2006">{{cite web|series=FQXi Awards|title=A. Garrett Lisi|date=July 31, 2006|website=[[FQXi]]|url=http://www.fqxi.org/large-grants/awardee/details/lisi|access-date=July 5, 2008|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080706043045/http://www.fqxi.org/large-grants/awardee/details/lisi|archive-date=6 July 2008}}</ref> In June 2007, Lisi thought that the algebraic structure he had constructed in an attempt to unify the [[Standard Model]] of particle physics with [[general relativity]] partially matched part of the algebraic structure of the [[E8 (mathematics)|E{{sub|8}}]] [[Lie group]].<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Zeeya|last=Merali|title=Is mathematical pattern the theory of everything?|magazine=[[New Scientist]]|url=https://www.newscientist.com/channel/fundamentals/dn12891-is-mathematical-pattern-the-theory-of-everything.html|date=November 15, 2007|access-date=June 15, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080512055932/http://www.newscientist.com/channel/fundamentals/dn12891-is-mathematical-pattern-the-theory-of-everything.html|archive-date=12 May 2008|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Highfield-2007">{{cite news|first=Roger|last=Highfield|author-link=Roger Highfield|date=November 14, 2007|title=Surfer dude stuns physicists with theory of everything|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|place=London, UK|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/earth/main.jhtml?view=DETAILS&grid=&xml=/earth/2007/11/14/scisurf114.xml|url-status=dead|access-date=June 15, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080520050752/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/earth/main.jhtml?view=DETAILS&grid=&xml=%2Fearth%2F2007%2F11%2F14%2Fscisurf114.xml|archive-date=May 20, 2008}}</ref> In July 2007.<ref name="Lisi-1999">{{cite web|last=Lisi|first=Antony Garrett|date=October 13, 1999|title=The Mauitian Chronicles|url=http://li.si/JournalG/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080720063413/http://sifter.org/~aglisi/JournalG/|archive-date=20 July 2008|access-date=July 2, 2008}}</ref>

Lisi's paper, "[[An Exceptionally Simple Theory of Everything]]",<ref name=Lisi-2007/> was posted to the [[arXiv]] on 6 November 2007. His theory was discussed on major physics [[blogs]]<ref name=Weatherall-2008/> and reported by media sources in several countries.<ref name=Porter-2010>{{cite news|first=Mitch|last=Porter|date=January 30, 2010|title=Surfer inspires comparisons to Albert Einstein|newspaper=[[The Toronto Star]]|url=https://www.thestar.com/news/world/article/758043--surfer-inspires-comparisons-to-albert-einstein?bn=1#article|access-date=January 13, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|title=Geometry is all|date=November 22, 2007|magazine=[[The Economist (magazine)|The Economist]]|url=https://www.economist.com/science/displaystory.cfm?story_id=10170958|access-date=June 15, 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|date=February 26, 2008|title=Could the next Einstein be a surfer dude?|magazine=[[Discover Magazine]]|url=http://discovermagazine.com/2008/mar/13-e-nste-n|access-date=June 15, 2008|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080509191408/http://discovermagazine.com/2008/mar/13-e-nste-n|archive-date=9 May 2008}}</ref> Lisi presented his theory at the [[TED (conference)|TED Conference]] on 28 February 2008,<ref name=Lisi-TED-2008>{{cite web|first=A.G.|last=Lisi|date=February 28, 2008|title=Garrett Lisi profile|website=TED talks|url=https://www.ted.com/speakers/garrett_lisi|access-date=October 17, 2008|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081018041938/http://www.ted.com/index.php/speakers/garrett_lisi.html|archive-date=18 October 2008}}</ref> and has since presented several academic talks and colloquia.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Greg|last=Boustead|date=November 17, 2008|title=Garrett Lisi's exceptional approach to everything|magazine=SEED Magazine|url=http://seedmagazine.com/news/2008/11/garrett_lisis_exceptional_appr.php|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090202122533/http://www.seedmagazine.com/news/2008/11/garrett_lisis_exceptional_appr.php|url-status=unfit|archive-date=February 2, 2009}}</ref> The theory has been extensively criticized in the scientific community.<ref name="Collins-2008-03" /><ref name="Distler-Garibaldi-2010" /> Back in 2008, ''[[Scientific American]]'' stated, "Today the theory is being largely but not entirely ignored".<ref name="Collins-2008-03" /> 

In July 2009, at a FQXi conference in the Azores, Lisi made a public bet with [[Frank Wilczek]] that [[Superpartner|superparticles]] would not be detected by 8 July 2015.<ref name="bet">{{cite web|title=Science Pond|first=A.G.|last=Lisi|date=August 8, 2009|website=Science Pond|url=http://sciencepond.com/garrettlisi/statuses/2533216255|access-date=December 13, 2009}}{{dead link|date=January 2017|bot=InternetArchiveBot|fix-attempted=yes}}</ref> After a one-year extension to allow for more data collection from the [[Large Hadron Collider]], Frank Wilczek conceded the superparticle bet to Lisi in 2016.<ref name="bet2">{{cite magazine|title=Surfer physicist wins superparticle bet with Nobel laureate|magazine=[[New Scientist]]|url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/2101550-surfer-physicist-wins-superparticle-bet-with-nobel-laureate/|access-date=August 22, 2016}}</ref>

==''Invention USA''==
In 2011 and 2012, Lisi co-hosted ''[[Invention USA]]'' (with Reichart von Wolfsheild), a two-season, reality TV series on the [[History (U.S. TV channel)|History channel]].<ref name="Conroy-2011">{{cite magazine|first=Tom|last=Conroy|date=December 8, 2011|title=''Invention USA'', a chance to dream|magazine=[[Media Life Magazine]]|url=http://www.medialifemagazine.com/artman2/publish/TV_Reviews_21/-Invention-USA-a-chance-to-dream.asp|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 28, 2013|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130128125106/http://www.medialifemagazine.com/artman2/publish/TV_Reviews_21/-Invention-USA-a-chance-to-dream.asp|access-date=20 December 2011}}</ref> Lisi was replaced as co-host by Scotty Ziegler in the second season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tvtango.com/series/invention_usa|title=Invention USA|website=TV Tango}}</ref>

== Pacific Science Institute ==
Lisi founded the Pacific Science Institute (PSI), an organization established to support independent scientific research and collaboration outside traditional academic institutions. Its first site on [[Maui]] was acquired in 2013 and made available to visiting researchers. A second site in [[Utah]] was established in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Horgan |first=John |title=Surfer-Physicist Offers Alternative to String Theory, Academia |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/blog/cross-check/surfer-physicist-offers-alternative-to-string-theory-academia/ |access-date=2026-10-11 |website=Scientific American |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=About {{!}} Pacific Science Institute |url=https://www.pacificscienceinstitute.org/about.html |access-date=2026-10-11 |website=www.pacificscienceinstitute.org}}</ref>

==Research==
Lisi has worked as an independent researcher in [[theoretical physics]], focusing on [[differential geometry]] and [[Lie algebras]] and their applications to gravity and [[particle physics]]. His research has explored geometric frameworks for combining general relativity with the [[Standard Model of particle physics]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weatherall |first=A. Garrett Lisi, James Owen |date=2014-08-01 |title=Garrett Lisi Explains His Grand Unified Theory |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/garrett-lisi-explains-his-grand-unified-theory/ |access-date=2026-10-11 |website=Scientific American |language=en}}</ref>

His research has been supported by the [[Foundational Questions Institute]] (FQXi).<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wallace-Wells |first=Benjamin |date=2008-07-24 |title=Surfing the Universe |url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2008/07/21/surfing-the-universe |access-date=2026-10-11 |work=The New Yorker |language=en-US |issn=0028-792X}}</ref>

===Quantum mechanics===
On 8 May 2006, in an arXiv preprint, "Quantum mechanics from a universal action reservoir,"<ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Lisi|first1=A. Garrett|year=2006|title=Quantum mechanics from a universal action reservoir|eprint=physics/0605068 }}</ref> Lisi proposed that the [[path integral formulation]] of [[quantum mechanics]] can be derived from [[information theory]] and the existence of a universal action reservoir.<ref>{{cite web|title=This could end the String Theory industry|access-date=July 6, 2008|first=John|last=Reilly|date=November 17, 2007|series=The Long View|url=http://www.johnreilly.info/17Nov07.htm|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090529022918/http://www.johnreilly.info/17Nov07.htm|archive-date=May 29, 2009}}</ref>

===An Exceptionally Simple Theory of Everything===
{{Main|An Exceptionally Simple Theory of Everything}}

Lisi's main work in theoretical physics is his [[An Exceptionally Simple Theory of Everything|Exceptionally Simple Theory of Everything]]. It proposes a [[unified field theory]] combining a [[grand unification theory]] of [[particle physics]] with [[Albert Einstein]]'s [[general relativity|general relativistic]] description of [[gravitation]], using the largest [[simple group|simple]] [[exceptional Lie algebra]], [[E8 (mathematics)|E{{sub|8}}]].<ref name="Lisi-2007">{{cite arXiv|last=Lisi|first=A. Garrett|year=2007|title=An exceptionally simple theory of everything|eprint=0711.0770|class=hep-th}}</ref><ref name="Lisi-Weatherall-2010">{{cite magazine|first1=A.G.|last1=Lisi|first2=James Owen|last2=Weatherall|name-list-style=amp|year=2010|title=A geometric theory of everything|magazine=[[Scientific American]]|volume=303|issue=6|pages=30–37|url=http://www.scientificamerican.com/article.cfm?id=a-geometric-theory-of-everything|doi=10.1038/scientificamerican1210-54|pmid=21141358|bibcode=2010SciAm.303f..54L}}</ref> Lisi stated that [[gravitation|gravity]], the [[Standard Model]] [[bosons]] and [[fermions]] can be unified as parts of an [[E8 (mathematics)|E{{sub|8}}]] superconnection. The theory, called ''E{{sub|8}} Theory'', also predicts the existence of many new particles.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ten Quick Questions with … Garrett Lisi|date=March 1, 2008|series=Science Channel|url=http://science.discovery.com/questions/garrett-lisi/garrett-lisi.html|access-date=July 2, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080605120207/http://science.discovery.com/questions/garrett-lisi/garrett-lisi.html|archive-date=5 June 2008|url-status=live}}</ref> He then designed a web application, the ''Elementary Particle Explorer'',<ref name="Gardner-2008">{{cite web|first1=Garrett|last1=Lisi|first2=Troy|last2=Gardner|first3=Greg|last3=Little|name-list-style=amp|date=August 9, 2008|title=Elementary Particle Explorer|website=Deferential Geometry|url=http://deferentialgeometry.org/epe/|url-status=live|access-date=September 4, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080917174018/http://deferentialgeometry.org/epe/|archive-date=17 September 2008}}</ref> for visualizing the charge structure of the elementary particles in the standard model, in grand unified theories, and in E{{sub|8}} Theory.

Lisi's theory has been extensively criticized in the scientific community.<ref name="cbc-2007-11-16" /><ref name="Collins-2008-03" /><ref name="Distler-Garibaldi-2010" /> Lisi acknowledges that his theory is incomplete. In a ''[[Scientific American]]'' post, Lisi stated, "(the 3 generation) … issue remains the most significant problem, and until it is solved the theory is not complete and cannot be considered much more than a speculative proposal. Without fully describing how the three generations of fermions work, the theory and all predictions from it remain tenuous."<ref name="Lisi-2011">{{cite magazine|first=Garrett|last=Lisi|date=May 4, 2011|title=Garrett Lisi responds to criticisms|type=blog post|magazine=Scientific American|url=http://www.scientificamerican.com/blog/post.cfm?id=garrett-lisi-responds-to-criticisms-2011-05-04|access-date=June 2, 2011}}</ref>

In June 2010, Lisi posted "An explicit embedding of gravity and the Standard Model in E{{sub|8}}",<ref name="Lisi-2010">{{cite arXiv|last=Lisi|first=A. Garrett|year=2010|title=An explicit embedding of gravity and the Standard Model in E{{sub|8}}|eprint=1006.4908|class=hep-th}}</ref> and in 2015 an update and generalization, "Lie group cosmology",<ref name="Lisi1">{{Citation |last=Lisi |first=A. Garrett |title=Lie Group Cosmology |date=2015-09-24 |url=http://arxiv.org/abs/1506.08073 |access-date=2026-10-11 |publisher=arXiv |doi=10.48550/arXiv.1506.08073 |id=arXiv:1506.08073}}</ref> in which he claims to have solved the 3 generations problem. The 2015 paper remains unpublished.

=== Lie group cosmology ===
In 2015, Lisi proposed a cosmological model based on Lie groups. His paper examined how de Sitter spacetime can be embedded in Lie groups and how deforming Lie group geometry can give rise to a superconnection.<ref name="Lisi1" />

=== Triality ===
Lisi's later research has focused on triality, a symmetry in certain Lie groups and Clifford algebras. In his 2024 preprint C, P, T, and [[Triality]], he proposed extending charge conjugation, parity and time-reversal symmetries with a triality transformation. He introduced the [[CPT symmetry|CPTt]] group as a mathematical framework for relating the three generations of fermions, developing an idea also present in his earlier work on [[E8 (mathematics)|E8]].<ref name=":1">{{Citation |last=Lisi |first=A. Garrett |title=C, P, T, and Triality |date=2024-07-29 |url=http://arxiv.org/abs/2407.02497 |access-date=2026-10-11 |publisher=arXiv |doi=10.48550/arXiv.2407.02497 |id=arXiv:2407.02497}}</ref>

=== Division algebras ===
Lisi's research has examined the relationships among [[division algebras]], [[Clifford algebras]], [[spinors]], [[triality]], and [[Exceptional Lie algebra|exceptional Lie algebras]].<ref name="Lisi2">{{Cite journal |last=Lisi |first=A. Garrett |date=2026-08-29 |title=Division Algebras, Triality, and Exceptional Magic |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s00006-026-01447-5 |journal=Advances in Applied Clifford Algebras |volume=36 |issue=4 |doi=10.1007/s00006-026-01447-5 |issn=0188-7009}}</ref> His work focuses on [[mathematical structures]] including [[complex numbers]], [[quaternions]], [[octonions]], and related composition algebras to investigate the symmetries and representations underlying theoretical physics.  He has studied how these algebras relate to Clifford algebras and their associated symmetry groups, and how triality connects vector and spinor representations.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Merali |first=Zeeya |title=Is mathematical pattern the theory of everything? |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/1891486-is-mathematical-pattern-the-theory-of-everything/ |website=New Scientist}}</ref>

=== Algebraic structures in theoretical physics ===
Lisi's later work has examined the use of triality, [[division algebras]], Clifford algebras, and exceptional Lie groups in theoretical physics. His 2024 and 2026 publications focuses on mathematical relationships among these structures and their possible applications to particle physics, including the organization of fermion generations and the symmetries of physical theories. This work extends his earlier research on E8 and its proposed use in a unified framework for gravity and particle physics.<ref name=":1" /><ref name="Lisi2" />

=== A Geometric Theory of Everything ===
In December 2010, Lisi and [[James Owen Weatherall]] published “A Geometric Theory of Everything” in Scientific American. The article outlined Lisi's E8 proposal and its proposed application to the Standard Model of particle physics and gravity.<ref name="Lisi-Weatherall-2010" />
